walkthroughs.body_html:
Your hook is the first line.

Bad: 'Hi I'd like to talk about my idea…'

Good: 'One in three school bags break. We fix that for £10.'

Start with the problem and the fix. 🎯

A great pitch tells a story:

  • The problem.
  • Your solution.
  • Who the customer is.
  • How you'll make money.
  • What you need (£ or help).

Keep it under 2 minutes.

On Dragons' Den, founders ask for cash in exchange for equity — a share of the business.

'£20,000 for 20%' means the business is valued at £100,000.

Practise your elevator pitch — 30 seconds that nails it. ⏱️

mcqs.q: Why might a business adopt corporate social responsibility (CSR)?
options: CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.
CSR is purely about being ethical with no business benefit.
Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness only.
Reasons include genuine ethics, but also commercial benefits — improved reputation, customer loyalty, employee retention, and reduced regulatory or reputational risk.

mcqs.q: What are the four Ps of the marketing mix?
options: The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
Product, Price, Place (distribution), and Promotion — the controllable variables a business uses to satisfy customers and achieve objectives.
The four Ps are Product, Price, Profit, and People.
CSR is the legal requirement to pay taxes.

mcqs.q: Why are hygiene factors and motivators not on the same scale in Herzberg's theory?
options: The four Ps are Planning, Producing, Promoting, and Profit.
Hygiene factors are about workplace cleanliness only.
Hygiene factors and motivators are just two types of motivation that combine.

Hygiene factors only prevent dissatisfaction (their absence demotivates, presence is neutral); motivators create satisfaction (their presence motivates, absence is neutral). They affect different outcomes, not different points on one scale.
